criteria.criterion: The planning gate in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (grep `planned`) also holds when any accepted Behavior criterion text names 'fails without the fix', and the trigger is a small named helper with a doc comment, not inline string matching.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. The gate is now `let planned = ... p.plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_failing_run(&reading)) && !capability.pins_repo();`. `asks_for_failing_run` is a named function with a `///` doc comment. It keeps only Behavior criteria, lowercases the text and collapses whitespace, then compares it with the const `FAILING_RUN_PHRASES`. There is no inline string matching in dispatch.

findings.summary: The trigger matches a fixed list of phrases in free text, so some wordings with the same meaning are missed.
findings.evidence: FAILING_RUN_PHRASES holds 'fails/fail without the fix', 'fails without the change' and 'fails without the mechanism'. Plural forms such as 'tests fail without the change' and wordings such as 'fails on the base' do not match, so those jobs are still skipped. A missed match costs a missing demonstration; a false match only costs a plan. The more reliable fix is a structured flag the reader sets on each criterion, but the accepted reading put that field out of scope. A follow-up could add it.

findings.summary: The new CLI planned-job test checks the plan records but not the verifier prompt.
findings.evidence: `an_easy_job_with_a_fails_without_criterion_is_planned_under_the_repository_hard_mode` checks roles and plan files only. The core test is the one that checks the fails-without-1 record reaches the verifier, so criterion 1 is still met.

summary: The change does what the request asks. Planning used to be decided by `hard_reason` alone. The planning gate in run/mod.rs now also plans a job when an accepted Behavior criterion names a failing run without the fix. That check lives in a small documented helper, `asks_for_failing_run`. The rest of planning works as before: `enabled = false` still plans nothing, `mode = "all"` still plans every job, and a pinned repository is still never planned. I ran the four new core tests, the whole `run::tests` module (53 passed) and the CLI `job_plan` target (30 passed); all pass. The main new test drives an easy job through `Athena::go` and checks that the planner and critic run, that the plan and critique records are committed, and that the verifier prompt contains the `fails-without-1` record. Athena's revert run shows those tests failing without the fix (exit 101, roles Reader, Producer, Verifier). The ordinary-job guard passes on the revert run too, which is expected: it only catches over-widening. The existing mode tests in job_plan.rs are unchanged and still pass. The design doc and the changelog both state the new rule and its root cause. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. One minor soundness point: the trigger matches a fixed list of phrases in free text, so some plural wordings are missed. The reading already accepted that, because the criterion record has no fails_without field.
